title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 337 (Penalty for frauds by officers)

content.overview: If any person, being at the time of the commission of the alleged offence an officer of a company which is subsequently ordered to be wound up by the Tribunal or which subsequently passes a resolution for voluntary winding up, has by false pretences or other fraud induced any person to give credit to the company, or with intent to defraud creditors has made or caused to be made any gift or transfer of or charge on or caused or connived at the levying of any execution against the property of the company, or has concealed or removed any part of the property of the company since or within two months before the date of any unsatisfied judgment or order for payment of money obtained against the company, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees.
content.glance: Officers who by fraud induce credit, or with intent to defraud creditors gift/transfer/charge property or conceal property before an unsatisfied judgment, face 1–3 years’ imprisonment and fine.
content.study: Section 337 penalises specified frauds by officers of a company that is subsequently wound up. The person must have been an officer at the time of the alleged offence. The prohibited conduct includes inducing credit by false pretences or fraud; making gifts, transfers or charges on company property, or conniving at execution, with intent to defraud creditors; and concealing or removing property since or within two months before an unsatisfied judgment or order for payment. Punishment is imprisonment of not less than one year and up to three years, and fine of not less than one lakh and up to three lakh rupees.

sections.heading: Prohibited acts
sections.body: Inducing credit by false pretences/fraud; gifts/transfers/charges or connivance at execution with intent to defraud creditors; concealment/removal of property around unsatisfied judgment.

examples.title: Fraudulent inducement of credit
examples.body: A director induces a supplier to extend credit by false statements about the company’s solvency. The company is later ordered to be wound up. The director is liable under s. 337.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 337 require that the company already be in winding up when the fraud occurs?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The person must have been an officer at the time of the offence; the company is subsequently ordered to be wound up or passes a voluntary winding-up resolution.

misconceptions.trap: Only current directors can be prosecuted.
misconceptions.correction: The section applies to any person who was an officer at the time of the alleged offence.
